title: Bifibrant nerve presentation of derived right Quillen equivalences
statement:
Use simplicial model categories, bifibrant objects, the homotopy coherent nerve and infinity localizations of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the Quillen derived-adjunction conventions of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and the meaning of combinatorial from [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be a simplicial Quillen adjunction between combinatorial simplicial model categories. Assume it is a Quillen equivalence: for each cofibrant $X$ and fibrant $Y$, a map $LX\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $X\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Work in fixed universes, enlarged to contain the categories and nerves. Let $Q:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$ be a simplicially enriched functor and $q:Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal M}$ an enriched natural transformation such that every $QX$ is cofibrant and every $q_X:QX\to X$ is a trivial fibration. For any such choice, $QR$ restricts to a simplicial functor $\mathcal N^{cf}\to\mathcal M^{cf}$ and
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}(QR):N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal N^{cf})\longrightarrow N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})$$
is a categorical equivalence in the sense of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Under the localization equivalences of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], it represents $\mathbf R R$, including its action on mapping spaces and composition homotopies. The derived adjunction $\mathbf L L\dashv\mathbf R R$ has equivalence unit and counit. A trivial fibration means a fibration which is a weak equivalence; no preservation of cofibrant objects by $R$ is assumed.
